page: Microsoft Azure E2ds_v7 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine belonging to the Edsv7 server family. Powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz, this instance features 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled. The processor is equipped with 48 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a large 480 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, Intel AMX for tile and int8 operations, and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. The server is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core, and includes 118 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capability.

Benchmark evaluations indicate a clear performance profile. The single-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng at 2215.58, and the PassMark memory score of 1927.71 both rank in the average tier. However, multi-core CPU performance is weak, scoring 2263.98 on stress-ng, which reflects the physical limitation of its single-core, dual-thread design. Memory bandwidth benchmarks show weak to poor results, with read-only large block bandwidth at 22.92 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 12.15 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET operations also fall into the lower performance tiers, with Redis achieving 4.01 million operations per second. For lightweight machine learning tasks, the server achieves an average text generation speed of 88.94 tokens per second on a small 135M model, though prompt processing speeds remain weak.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E2ds_v7 offers a high memory density relative to its compute footprint, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing power. The inclusion of 118 GB of local storage and Premium Storage capability adds value for applications requiring fast local scratch space. The primary tradeoff is the limited multi-core processing capability and lower memory write bandwidth. This server is best suited for small-scale databases, caching layers, lightweight web serving, and memory-intensive development or testing environments.
